{{Short description|Award in applied mathematics}}
{{primary sources|date=January 2020}}
The '''AMS–SIAM Cathleen Synge Morawetz Prize in Applied Mathematics''' is awarded jointly by the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) in honor of [[Cathleen Synge Morawetz]].<ref name="AMS">{{citation | url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=9| title=AMS–SIAM Cathleen Synge Morawetz Prize in Applied Mathematics | publisher=American Mathematical Society | access-date=2026-02-21 }}</ref><ref>{{citation | url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/prizes-awards/joint-prizes/ams-siam-cathleen-synge-morawetz-prize-in-applied-mathematics/ | title=AMS–SIAM Cathleen Synge Morawetz Prize in Applied Mathematics | publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics | access-date=2026-02-21 }}</ref>  Prior to 2025, it was known as the AMS–SIAM George David Birkhoff Prize in Applied Mathematics, in honor of [[George David Birkhoff]].<ref name="AMS" /> It is currently awarded every three years for an outstanding contribution to "applied mathematics in the highest and broadest sense".<ref name="AMS" /> The recipient of the prize has to be a member of one of the awarding societies, as well as a resident of the [[United States]], [[Canada]], or [[Mexico]]. The prize was endowed in 1967 and first issued in 1968.  As of 2026, it amounts to [[US$]]5,000.<ref name="AMS" />

==Recipients==
{| class="wikitable sortable"
!Year
!Winner
!Reason
|-
|1968
|[[Jürgen Moser]]
|"for his contributions to the theory of Hamiltonian dynamical systems, especially his proof of the stability of periodic solutions of [[Hamiltonian system]]s having two degrees of freedom and his specific applications of the ideas in connection with this work."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Browse Prizes and Awards|url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/pabrowse.cgi?parent_id=9|website=American Mathematical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-05-09}}</ref>
|-
|1973
|[[James Serrin]] and [[Fritz John]]
|"for his outstanding work in [[partial differential equation]]s, in [[numerical analysis]], and, particularly, in nonlinear elasticity theory; the latter work has led to his study of quasi-isometric mappings as well as functions of bounded mean oscillation, which have had impact in other areas of analysis."<ref name=":0" />
|-
|1978
|[[Clifford Truesdell]], [[Mark Kac]], and [[Garrett Birkhoff]]
|"for bringing the methods of algebra and the highest standards of mathematics to scientific applications."<ref name=":0" />
|-
|1983
|[[Paul Garabedian]]
|"for his important contributions to partial differential equations, to the mathematical analysis of problems of [[transonic]] flow and airfoil design by the method of complexification, and to the development and application of scientific computing to problems of [[fluid dynamics]] and [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]]."<ref name=":0" />
|-
|1988
|[[Elliott H. Lieb]]
|"for his profound analysis of problems arising in [[mathematical physics]]."<ref name=":0" />
|-
|1994
|[[Ivo Babuška]] and [[S. R. Srinivasa Varadhan]]
|"to Ivo Babuška for important contributions to the reliability of [[finite element method]]s, the development of a general framework for finite element error estimation, and the development of p- and hp- finite element methods; and to S. R. S. Varadhan for important contributions to the martingale characterization of diffusion processes, to the theory of large deviations for functionals of occupation times of [[Markov chain|Markov processes]], and to the study of random media."<ref name=":0" />
|-
|1998
|[[Paul Rabinowitz]]
|"for his deep influence on the field of [[nonlinear analysis]]."<ref>{{Cite journal|date=April 1998|title=1998 Birkhoff Prize|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199804/comm-birkhoff-prize.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=45|pages=509–510}}</ref>
|-
|2003
|[[John N. Mather]] and [[Charles S. Peskin]]
|"to John Mather for being a mathematician of exceptional depth, power, and originality; and to Charles S. Peskin for devoting much of his career to understanding the dynamics of the human heart and bringing an extraordinarily broad range of expertise to bear on this problem."<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2003|title=2003 Birkhoff Prize|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200304/comm-birkhoff.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=50|pages=470–473}}</ref>
|-
|2006
|[[Cathleen Synge Morawetz]]
|"for her deep and influential work in partial differential equations, most notably in the study of [[shock wave]]s, transonic flow, scattering theory, and conformally invariant estimates for the [[wave equation]]."<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2006|title=2006 Birkhoff Prize|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200604/comm-birkhoff.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=53|pages=474}}</ref>
|-
|2009
|[[Joel Smoller]]
|"for his leadership, originality, depth, and breadth of work in dynamical systems, differential equations, [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|mathematical biology]], shock wave theory, and [[general relativity]]."<ref>{{Cite journal|date=April 2009|title=2009 AMS-SIAM Birkhoff Prize|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200904/rtx090400492p.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=56|pages=492–493}}</ref>
|-
|2012
|[[Björn Engquist]]
|"for his contributions to a wide range of powerful [[Computational mathematics|computational methods]] over more than three decades."<ref>{{Cite journal|date=April 2012|title=2012 AMS–SIAM Birkhoff Prize|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201204/rtx120400576p.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=59|pages=576–577}}</ref>
|-
|2015
|[[Emmanuel Candès]]
|"for his work on compressed sensing that has revolutionized [[signal processing]] and [[medical imaging]] and his related work on computational [[harmonic analysis]], statistics and scientific computing."<ref>{{Cite journal|date=April 2015|title=2015 AMS-SIAM Birkhoff Prize|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201504/rnoti-p423.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=62|pages=423–424}}</ref>
|-
|2018
|[[Bernd Sturmfels]]
|"for his instrumental role in creating the field of applied [[algebraic geometry]]."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bernd Sturmfels to Receive 2018 George David Birkhoff Prize in Applied Mathematics|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=3823|website=American Mathematical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-05-09}}</ref>
|-
|2021
|[[Gunther Uhlmann]]
|"for his fundamental and insightful contributions to [[inverse problem]]s and partial differential equations, as well as for his incisive work on boundary rigidity, microlocal analysis and cloaking."<ref>[https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6491 "2021 AMS-SIAM Birkhoff Prize"]</ref> 
|-
|2024
|[[Ronald Coifman]]
|"for his profound impact on pure and applied harmonic analysis, and for the introduction of tools developed from these areas to address modern challenges of [[data science]]."<ref>[http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7238 "2024 AMS-SIAM Birkhoff Prize"]</ref>
|}
